stances.claim: The 1987 Constitution improved the 1935 tripartite system by limiting presidential powers, strengthening Congress and the SC, and adding three independent commissions -- all lessons from the Marcos regime.
The ease of House indictment (1/3 vote) is deliberately checked and balanced by the difficulty of Senate conviction (2/3 vote or 16 senators) -- this is not a flaw but a design feature.

The Ombudsman can investigate impeachable officials even while they are in office -- for the purpose of filing a verified impeachment complaint in the House, recovering ill-gotten wealth, or prosecuting them criminally after their term.
The OMB is itself subject to impeachment -- 'every ombudsman is under fire from high officials' because of its broad authority.
Readers should wisely evaluate whether the forthcoming impeachment of Ombudsman Morales is a sincere effort to uphold accountability or a ploy for political vendetta.

notable_anecdotes: The 1/3 House indictment vs 2/3 Senate conviction asymmetry -- designed so that getting an indictment is relatively easy but conviction requires a supermajority: 16 of 24 senators.

The OMB's unique authority under RA 6770 to investigate impeachable officials and file verified impeachment complaints in the House -- a power that makes every ombudsman a target of officials they investigate.

The column's closing as a framing device for the forthcoming Ombudsman Morales impeachment -- asking whether it is 'a sincere effort to uphold accountability or a mere ploy to extract political vendetta.'

The 1987 Constitution's new accountability clause -- 'Public officers and employees must at all times be accountable to the people... lead modest lives' -- as a post-Marcos corrective that has no equivalent in the 1935 Constitution.

one_paragraph_summary: As preface to the forthcoming impeachment of Ombudsman Conchita Carpio Morales, Panganiban surveys the 1987 Constitution's accountability architecture. The 1987 framers improved the 1935 tripartite system -- using lessons from the Marcos regime -- by limiting presidential powers, strengthening Congress and the SC, and adding three independent commissions (Comelec, COA, CSC). The new accountability clause commands public officers to serve with 'utmost responsibility, integrity, loyalty, and efficiency... act with patriotism and justice, and lead modest lives.' Two accountability mechanisms operate in parallel. Congress can impeach and oust the president, VP, SC justices, three commission members, and the ombudsman -- the House initiates by 1/3 vote, the Senate convicts by 2/3 vote (16 senators); this asymmetry is a deliberate design feature, checked only by reason, equity, and the people's will. The OMB, through RA 6770's Sec. 15, has authority to investigate even impeachable officials for three purposes: (1) filing a verified impeachment complaint in the House, if warranted; (2) filing civil cases for ill-gotten wealth recovery; and (3) filing criminal indictments after the official has served. The OMB is checked by the Sandiganbayan and SC, and is itself subject to impeachment and subsequent criminal and civil suits -- which is why every ombudsman faces fire from the high officials it investigates. The closing call: readers should evaluate whether the Morales impeachment is 'a sincere effort to uphold accountability or a mere ploy to extract political vendetta.'
